title: [Suite autour de Teichmüller dont] Teichmülleries, 1981-1982 : notes manuscrites (1981-1983, s.d.), lettres (1981, s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Setting. Grothendieck is working with the cartographic groups. Π_{0,3} = ⟨ρ0, ρ1, ρ∞ | ρ0ρ1ρ∞ = 1⟩ is free of rank 2, i.e. π1(P^1 − {0,1,∞}). With ρ1² = 1 added it becomes the oriented cartographic group. Π^τ_{0,3} is the extension by an orientation-reversing involution τ. Finite (weighted, triangulated) maps correspond to finite sets with an action of these groups. The previous page imposed relations ρ_i^{ν_i} = 1, meaning that vertices of type i have order dividing ν_i. It noted that for ordinary maps ρ1^{ν1} with ν1 odd collapses to ρ1 = 1, giving only the trivial cyclotomic maps z ↦ z^n.

This page:
1. For ordinary maps, only the relations of type (30) are of interest, excluding (31).
2. The convention ρ_i^∞ = 1 means 'no relation'. So any triple ν_i ∈ N̄* = N* ∪ {+∞}, i ∈ {0,1,∞}, can be imposed.
3. The corresponding finite weighted triangular maps are exactly the finite sets with an action of:
   - (32) Π_{0,3}/⟨ρ0^{ν0}, ρ1^{ν1}, ρ∞^{ν∞}⟩, the orientation-preserving triangle group Δ(ν0, ν1, ν∞), in the oriented case;
   - (32 bis) the same quotient of Π^τ_{0,3}, the extended triangle (reflection) group, an extension of {1,τ} by (32), in the non-oriented case.
4. (33) identifies the triangle group with a 'fundamental group with signature' π1(P^1(C), ν_*; P_+), where ν_* = ν0R0 + ν1R1 + ν∞R∞ is a signature (weighted divisor) on P^1_C. Equivalently it is the fundamental group of the 'multiplicité' (orbifold / stack) P^1 with cone points of orders ν_i, with ν_i = ∞ meaning a puncture.
5. This holds in the topological, analytic or schematic setting; in the schematic case one gets the profinite completion.

Next page. Grothendieck defines the multiplicity as the topos of ramified coverings with prescribed indices, plus a 'mixed topos' with the {1,τ} action for the non-orientable case. He then identifies the profinite completions with étale π1 of the stacky P^1 over C or Q̄, and over R or Q̄∩R.

In modern terms: Belyi maps (dessins) of type (ν0, ν1, ν∞) correspond to finite-index subgroups of the triangle group, i.e. to finite étale covers of the orbifold/stacky curve P^1(ν0, ν1, ν∞). Real structures correspond to the extended triangle group. This serves his program of studying the Galois action on dessins, stratified by signature.
errors: The equation number (31) is reused: the previous page already uses (31) for ρ1^{ν1} = 1, and here it labels ν_i ∈ N̄*. This is a harmless numbering slip.

There is an implicit gap: for 'bad' signatures, e.g. (p, q, 1) with p ≠ q, the multiplicity is not uniformized by a surface. The identification (33) still holds formally: the quotient group is cyclic of order gcd(p, q), and the orbifold π1 agrees. But the claim on the next page that the topos is 'locally a surface' should be read stack-theoretically. No real error.

ideas.what: Imposing ρ_i^{ν_i} = 1, with ν_i ∈ N* ∪ {∞}, on the cartographic group; maps of given type correspond to actions of the triangle group Δ(ν0, ν1, ν∞).
ideas.modern_name: Triangle groups as quotients of the (oriented/extended) cartographic group; maps and hypermaps of type (p,q,r)
ideas.usually_credited_to: Jones–Singerman (1978), Theory of maps on orientable surfaces; also Coxeter and others for regular maps
ideas.where_published: Esquisse d'un programme (1984), section on dessins and cartographic groups, in general terms

ideas.what: Identification of the triangle group with the fundamental group 'with signature' of P^1 with cone points of orders ν_i, viewed as the π1 of a 'multiplicité' (topos).
ideas.modern_name: Orbifold fundamental group / fundamental group of a stacky curve P^1(ν0, ν1, ν∞)
ideas.usually_credited_to: Thurston (orbifolds, 1978); Fuchsian groups with signature (Poincaré, Fricke–Klein); stack-theoretic version Noohi (2004), Behrend–Noohi
ideas.where_published: Esquisse mentions 'multiplicités' (modular multiplicities) but not, to my knowledge, this explicit signature formula

ideas.what: The non-oriented case: the extended triangle group is the π1 of a mixed topos (the multiplicity with its complex-conjugation action). Its profinite completion is the étale π1 of the stacky P^1 over R (or Q̄∩R).
ideas.modern_name: Extended triangle groups ↔ real (Klein-surface) dessins; étale π1 of real stacky curves
ideas.usually_credited_to: Köck–Singerman (real Belyi theory); Jones–Singerman; Cirre et al.
ideas.where_published: Esquisse discusses the {1,τ} / non-oriented cartographic group in general terms

ideas.what: In the schematic setting the fundamental group of the multiplicity is the profinite completion of the triangle group.
ideas.modern_name: Étale fundamental group of root stacks / tame π1 with bounded ramification
ideas.usually_credited_to: SGA1 (tame π1, Grothendieck–Murre); Noohi for stacks
ideas.where_published: SGA1 and Grothendieck–Murre (tame fundamental group, bounded ramification indices)

missed.claim: Grothendieck treats orbifold/stacky P^1 with signature as a topos ('multiplicité') whose π1 is the triangle group, uniformly in the topological, analytic and schematic settings. He includes an orientation-reversing 'mixed topos' for the real case. This is an early (1981) stack-theoretic formulation of orbifold fundamental groups of signature curves. It predates its standard appearance (Noohi, Behrend–Noohi), but the content is well known today.
missed.quote: ou encore comme groupe fondamental de la multiplicité (topologique, analytique ou schématique, au choix — mais dans ce dernier cas il s'agit du compactifié profini ...)
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: Historical priority only: it documents Grothendieck's early stacky viewpoint on dessins of a given type. There is no new mathematics for specialists.

deep.surprise_reason: The content (triangle groups, extended triangle groups, orbifold fundamental groups, profinite completions as étale π1 of stacky curves) is standard. Only the early topos/'multiplicité' formulation, including the real non-orientable mixed topos, is a mildly interesting historical detail.
transcription_corrections: Line 2–3 likely reads: 'les relations intéressantes à considérer sont du type (30), à l'exclusion de (31)'. The '(*)' should be '(31)', referring to ρ1^{ν1} = 1 from the previous page.
'On considère que li[?]' should read 'On convient que l'on [pose] ρ_i^∞ = 1 par définition'; the crossed-out words are 'les cartes'.
'Les cartes (finies) paraboliques [?] triangulaires' should likely be 'Les cartes (finies) pondérées triangulaires', consistent with 'carte triangulée pondérée' on the previous page.
'qui s'identifie à une extension de {1,τ} par (32)' is correct. 'groupe fondamental "avec signature"' is correct.
In (33) the generators are ρ_i (written ρ), and the base point is P_+.
